name: Complementary eyeshadow for iris color
lead: Complementary eyeshadow for iris color is a makeup approach in which shadow shades are chosen from the opposite side of the color wheel to the iris, so the eye color looks more vivid. Practitioners commonly pair warm copper, bronze and brown tones with blue eyes, purples and plums with green or hazel eyes, and blue or navy tones with brown eyes.

People use it as a low-cost way to make eyes the focal point of the face without changing the eyes themselves. Eye shadow in general is described as able to work with eye color to enhance the look, add depth or draw attention to the eyes [1]. Forum posts discussing appearance advice mention that colors can make blue eyes "pop" [2].
No published trials have tested whether complementary shades change perceived attractiveness; the idea comes from color theory and makeup-artist practice.

chain: Pick a shade opposite the iris on the color wheel
Contrast makes the iris color look more saturated
angle.text: Shadow in a complementary hue sits next to the iris and heightens its apparent color through contrast. It is applied in minutes and washes off, so people use it to try different looks.

paras: The approach starts from the iris color and selects shades that contrast with it. Common pairings cited by makeup artists are orange-brown and bronze for blue eyes, plum and burgundy for green eyes, and navy, teal or violet for brown eyes. Grey and hazel eyes are often matched to whichever flecks the wearer wants to emphasize.
Shadow may be applied across the lid, on the outer corner or as a liner along the lash line, which keeps the contrast close to the iris.

Style discussions on forums treat eye color as a feature to be highlighted with surrounding colors, including hair color and makeup [2]. Such advice is mostly given for women's makeup, though the same color logic is used in cosmetic guides generally.

lore.intro: Forum participants mention that surrounding colors can make eye color stand out [2].

claims.believers: Posters say warmer hair and makeup colors make blue eyes stand out more [2].
claims.experts: No published studies have tested complementary shadow against perceived eye color or attractiveness.

card.summary: Choosing eyeshadow shades opposite the iris on the color wheel so eye color looks more vivid.

quick.overview:
Complementary eyeshadow means picking shadow colors that contrast with your iris color: warm bronzes and coppers for blue eyes, plums for green, blues and purples for brown.

It is a quick, reversible way to make the eyes the focal point of a face.
quick.mechanism: Colors opposite each other on the color wheel intensify one another when placed side by side, so the shadow makes the neighboring iris look more saturated.
quick.risks: Cosmetic eye products carry the usual risks of irritation or allergic reaction. No studies have measured the effect on perceived attractiveness.
